- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, cap forecast peak at 1–2% below true peak to avoid overshoot.
- When true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (especially in first 5–7 days), model may be overconfident; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day until mean reversion.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is high, model may be ignoring sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment rises.
- Model often overestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) prices; apply 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment for days 25–30 of forecast horizon.
- If sentiment history shows strong upward trend, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0% per day to align with sentiment momentum.
- When true outcome is consistently below 75% of forecast, model may be overfitting recent data; apply 1–2% downward correction for next 3–5 days.
